ch.s: Verses 1–10: “They walked in the midst of the fire, praising God, and blessing the Lord.”; Verses 11–20: “Don’t utterly deliver us up, for your name’s sake. Don’t annul your covenant.”; Verses 21–30: “Let them be ashamed of all their power and might, and let their strength be broken.”; Verses 31–40: “Blessed are you in the temple of your holy glory, to be praised and glorified above all forever!”; Verses 41–50: “O you stars of heaven, bless the Lord! Praise and exalt him above all forever!”; Verses 51–60: “O you lightnings and clouds, bless the Lord! Praise and exalt him above all forever!”; Verses 61–68: “O let Israel bless the Lord! Praise and exalt him above all forever.”. People named: Abraham, Isaac, Hananiah, Mishael, Azariah. Places: Jerusalem, Hades.
q: Read verses 1–10. What is happening, and what stands out to you most?
In verses 11–20, what do you learn about worship and praise?
Read verse 66 slowly. What does it say about God, about people, and about how to live?
What does Abraham’s part in this chapter teach you — as an example to follow or a warning to heed?
Where do you see the theme of promise and blessing in this chapter, and how does it connect to the rest of Prayer of Azariah?
What is one specific way you can put this chapter into practice this week?
ch.a: Write down three things this chapter shows about God and thank Him for each.
